assay_targets_or_enrichments.ontology_label: Chemical cross-linking coupled with mass spectrometry proteomics

acquisition: full-scan MS spectra from 375 to 1600 Da were acquired in the Orbitrap
Only peptides with charged states 3–8 were fragmented, and dynamic exclusion properties were set to n = 1
Fragmentation was performed using in a stepped HCD collision energy mode
labeling: no mention of TMT, SILAC, or other isotopic labels for the XL-MS runs
enrichment: treated with an optimised concentration of PhoX cross-linker

Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The study employs multiple MS modes: Bottom-up XL-MS (DDA), Middle-down MS, and Native Top-down MS. The primary proteomics dataset described in the PRIDE metadata and detailed LC-MS methods refers to the Bottom-up XL-MS workflow using the PhoX cross-linker and IMAC enrichment. Phosphorylation was specifically matched as an 80 Da variable modification in the middle-down analysis.

scope: HTT and HTT-HAP40 protein samples were expressed in insect cells and purified
HTT protein samples were purified by FLAG-affinity chromatography.
HTT-HAP40 samples were further purified with an additional Ni-affinity chromatography step prior to gel filtration.
For cross-linking experiments, HTT-HAP40 samples (HTTQ23-HAP40, HTTQ54-HAP40, HTT Δexon 1-HAP40) were diluted to a protein concentration of 1 mg/1 mL
Protein digestion was performed in 100 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.5, 1% SDC, 5 mM TCEP and 30 mM CAA, with the addition of Lys-C and Trypsin proteases

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The proteomics analysis (XL-MS, native MS, and middle-down MS) was performed on recombinant HTT and HTT-HAP40 complexes purified via FLAG and Ni-affinity chromatography from insect cells.

While the text mentions in vivo mouse knockouts and branaplam treatment in RPE1 cells, these were analyzed via Western Blot and qPCR, not the mass spectrometry proteomics described in the PRIDE metadata and LC-MS sections.
